parties: BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited; Gaurav Singh Kushwaha
headline: BlueStone Jewellery substantial shareholder disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Gaurav Singh Kushwaha has disclosed a substantial acquisition of shares in BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI Takeover Code 2011, triggering public disclosure obligations.
implication: A Regulation 31(4) disclosure signals either a crossing of the 5% threshold or a material change in shareholding by an identified acquirer—partners should monitor whether this precedes a formal EoI/offer under the Takeover Regulations.
detail: Gaurav Singh Kushwaha has filed a mandatory disclosure with NSE under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, concerning BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Limited. Regulation 31(4) requires disclosure when an acquirer crosses statutory thresholds (typically 5% or 10% of shareholding) or when shareholding changes materially post-announcement. The disclosure was submitted to the exchange on or around 24 June 2026. No valuation, consideration structure, or offer document has been publicly disclosed at this stage.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisition or change in control; triggers public announcement and transparency obligations.
Definition and thresholds for 'acquisition' (5% and 10% triggers); determines if formal open offer required.
Conditions precedent and approval framework; CCI clearance, credit approvals, and regulatory approvals.
Open offer structure, pricing, and consideration mechanics once threshold crossed.
CCI notification and approval if acquisition qualifies as 'combination' (turnover/asset thresholds).
Voting rights restrictions; nominee shareholding and disclosure of beneficial ownership.
Continuing disclosure, material event reporting, and shareholder approval for change of control.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 — Schedule I, Part C
framework.note: If acquirer is resident Indian, no FEMA approval typically required; if NRI/foreign, FPI/PIS routes apply.

conditions: Filing of disclosure under Regulation 31(4) within two trading days of crossing threshold
Material change in shareholding post-announcement compliance
approvals: CCI clearance (if acquisition qualifies as combination under Competition Act)
Stock exchange vetting and public announcement
Likely: open offer to public shareholders if 26% or 51% threshold breached (depending on initial holding)
structure.novel: No novel structure disclosed; this is a threshold disclosure step.

triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure when substantial share acquisition identified or shareholding materially changes.
Possible CCI 'combination' notification if acquirer's turnover/asset base crosses statutory thresholds.
If disclosure confirms crossing 5% or 10%, formal open offer likely triggered under Reg. 37–38.
